content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim in turn: the root cause is attributed to F1 but not yet verified, and the plain-words explanation is hedged as "likely" and backed by F1 and P1. The at-risk note relies on Code-Fix's reading, which F1 and M1 support, and the symptom that account pages failed for many shoppers is backed by Gbac1 and G5309. I'm now on the causal chain, where the share of failed requests appears to rise sharply.

I'm now checking the evidence for the causal chain: a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py shows up from 03:46 through the end of the logs read at 03:52, and the flag went from fully off, to mixed at 03:46, to fully on right after. I'm also confirming the rule-outs, since the only change event the day before was this flag switch with no deploy, and the account page error rate was still low before 03:46.

I'm going through the remaining claims: the contributing factors hold up, since the flag reached all of the account page's traffic within a minute, and the lack of a staged rollout or error-rate check is only an absence in the evidence. Whether a test existed is also only inferred from the absence of one. I'm leaving the action items and the what-if question unjudged.

supported.quote: The function the flag turned on, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, divides the account's total spent this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month` and has no answer for an empty list.

For any shopper who has bought before but not this month it raises ZeroDivisionError at the line the logs name, so every account page request for such a shopper failed once monthly-spend-feature sent the page's spend figure through it. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

Switching on a new feature made the account page use a new monthly spending calculation, and that calculation likely breaks for any shopper who has bought nothing this month because it ends up dividing by zero.

Code-Fix's reading says the faulty calculation was still in the code: switching monthly-spend-feature back on before a fix is in place could make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month, and with the flag off, the older calculation can still fail for accounts with no purchases at all.
Account pages failed for many shoppers
Shoppers opening their account page got a failed request instead of the page, and the service's share of failed requests rose sharply.
Account page requests were failing with ZeroDivisionError: division by zero, raised in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. The error shows up in the logs from the onset until the logs that were read end.
The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on by admin at {P1.1}. The flag's evaluations went from all off, to a mix of on and off at the onset, to all on right after it.
A deployment: the production change events read back for the day before the onset held only this flag change, and no deploy came back.
Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed only one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read, and that was this one.
The client-disconnect failures on the account page: these were seen before the onset, while the account page error rate was still low. The division-by-zero failures appear only once the flag went on.

With the flag on, the account page's spend figure goes through a new monthly per-item average that divides by the number of this month's purchases, and that number is zero for shoppers who have bought before but not this month.

The flag switch reached all of the account page's traffic at once: its evaluations went from all off to all on almost immediately. No staged rollout and no error-rate check that would halt it were seen.
Before the flag was switched on in production, no test was seen that ran the flag-on code path for a shopper with no purchases in the current month.
